issues.legal_issue: A party that categorically elects not to accept partial performance cannot later reverse that election and obtain specific performance of the performable part.
material_facts: The agreement required completion by a specified date, including mutation of the seller’s name in the land records and delivery of possession.
The seller could not deliver possession because another claimant’s suit and interim injunction prevented it, but she offered to execute and register the sale deed without delivering possession.
On the agreed date, the purchaser refused to proceed without possession and mutation, did not pay the remaining consideration, and did not relinquish claims to performance of the omitted part.
After the trial court refused specific performance and ordered a refund and compensation, the purchaser later offered in the first appeal to accept a sale deed without possession.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser’s categorical refusal to accept partial performance was an election that could not be reversed later; he was not entitled to specific performance of the performable part.
issues.legal_principle: Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 12(3) permits specific performance of the performable part in the stated circumstances only if the other party pays the required consideration and relinquishes claims to the omitted part and compensation. A party who has categorically refused partial performance cannot later resile from that election; a mere assertion that the whole contract should be performed, or a suit seeking whole performance without more, does not necessarily constitute such an election. The court recognized the broad proposition that an option to accept part performance may be exercised during litigation, citing Kalyanpur Lime Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar, Dr. Jiwan Lal v. Brij Mohan Mehra, Ram Niwas v. Smt. Omkari, Smt. T.K. Santha v. Smt. A.G. Rathnam, Ramani Ammal v. Susilammal, and Smt. Purnima Rani Dutta v. Smt. Lakshmi Bala Dasi, but distinguished those cases because no prior election against part performance had been made in them.

rule.if: specific_performance_claim and contract_unperformable_in_part and categorical_rejection_of_part_performance and (not whole_consideration_paid or not claims_to_omitted_part_relinquished)

predicates.specific_performance_claim: A party seeks specific performance of a contract.
predicates.contract_unperformable_in_part: A party to the contract cannot perform part of the promised performance.
predicates.categorical_rejection_of_part_performanc: The claimant unambiguously refuses to accept performance of the contract without the part that cannot be performed.
predicates.whole_consideration_paid: The claimant pays the consideration required for the contract as a whole, without abatement.
predicates.claims_to_omitted_part_relinquished: The claimant gives up claims to performance of the omitted part and compensation for its omission.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeking specific performance unambiguously rejects partial performance of a contract that cannot be fully performed, and has not satisfied the applicable payment or relinquishment conditions, the claimant cannot later accept partial performance.

issues.legal_issue: For a contract that cannot be performed in full, readiness and willingness to perform throughout must include willingness to accept the available partial performance.
material_facts: The seller could not deliver possession, making full performance of the agreement unavailable.
The purchaser refused on the agreed date to complete the sale without possession, despite the seller’s offer to execute and register the sale deed.
The purchaser offered to accept the sale deed without possession only later, during the first appeal.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser’s refusal to accept partial performance meant that he was not ready and willing at all stages to accept that performance, so he could not obtain specific performance of part of the contract later.
issues.legal_principle: The court stated that specific performance cannot be granted unless the claimant is ready and willing at all stages to perform. When the contract cannot be performed in full, that continuing readiness and willingness must be readiness and willingness to accept partial performance. A clear indication that the claimant will not accept partial performance defeats that requirement. The judgment discusses this principle in connection with Section 12(3) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963; it cites no separate earlier case for this readiness-and-willingness proposition.

predicates.specific_performance_claim: A party seeks specific performance of a contract.
predicates.contract_unperformable_in_part: A party to the contract cannot perform part of the promised performance.
predicates.claimant_clearly_unwilling_to_accept_par: The claimant clearly indicates that the claimant will not accept the performance that remains available.

issues.definition: A claimant seeking specific performance of a contract that cannot be fully performed is not ready and willing for partial performance if the claimant clearly refuses to accept it.

issues.legal_issue: When a sale agreement provides for double the advance if the seller does not complete the sale, that contractual remedy must be given effect when specific performance is refused and the purchaser has claimed the alternative compensation.
material_facts: The agreement provided that if the seller did not get the sale deed executed, the purchaser could seek execution through court or claim double the advance paid.
The purchaser claimed compensation in the alternative to specific performance.
The trial court refused specific performance but ordered repayment of the advance and a smaller amount of damages without explaining why the contractual double-advance term should not apply.
issues.conclusion: The decree was varied to require repayment of the advance with interest and payment of an additional equal amount with interest, giving effect to the agreement’s double-advance term.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the express term of the sale agreement providing for double the advance if the seller did not get the sale deed executed. It held that the trial court had given no reason for failing to give effect to that term or for awarding less compensation than the agreement specified. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this ruling.

predicates.specific_performance_refused: The court refuses the claimant’s request for specific performance.
predicates.alternative_compensation_claimed: The claimant seeks compensation as an alternative remedy.
predicates.agreement_stipulates_double_advance_on_n: The agreement provides for payment of double the advance if the seller does not complete the sale.

issues.definition: If specific performance is refused, the claimant has sought compensation instead, and the agreement provides for double the advance on noncompletion, the seller must pay that stipulated amount.
